name: SkinKey: one skin scan you can bring to Flipkart, Amazon and the pharmacy counter. Working title: the user's 'Skin Passport' is renamed because ShelfSense already uses that name. Module names: Skin Profile, Skin Forecast, Aisle Check.
one_liner: An Android app that sits in the share sheet of the Flipkart and Amazon.in apps. You scan your face once with YouCam Skin Analysis and Facial Color Tones, and the phone keeps only the derived scores. After that, sharing any skincare product into SkinKey returns 'fits / caution / unknown' with reasons tied to your scores. One tap opens Flipkart already filtered to your skin type (or a skin-keyword search on Amazon.in or Nykaa). A local UV and humidity card and an in-store barcode check with a pharmacist referral reuse the same profile.
target_user: Indian skincare shoppers aged 18-35 who buy on the Flipkart and Amazon.in Android apps (and Nykaa). Most don't know their skin type or ingredients: 70% don't know their skin type and 80% don't know ingredients (CeraVe/OnePoll 2021, vendor); 63% are wrong about their skin type (Labskin 2022, vendor). Secondary user: the same shopper at a chemist or pharmacy aisle, and the pharmacist they show their profile to.
buyer: Shopper-first and free for the demo. Retailer angle, pitched as a hypothesis and not a measured result: pharmacies and parapharmacies could use a revocable profile QR instead of running their own scanner. Precedent: Amazon opened a Milan parapharmacy with a Perfect Corp skin-analysis Derma-bar in Feb 2025 (premiumbeautynews, verified by research). There is no affiliate revenue in the hackathon build. Amazon Associates India bans Special Links in mobile apps unless the app gets separate approval (policy rule 7, agreement rule 21). Flipkart affiliate sign-up status is UNVERIFIED.
problem_evidence:
Verified:
- Shoppers often don't know their skin type or ingredients: 70% / 80% (CeraVe/OnePoll 2021, vendor) and 63% wrong (Labskin 2022, vendor).
- 49% have skincare unopened for over a year (HK Consumer Council 2021), which suggests mismatched purchases. That link is a hypothesis.
- Among 356 hackathon repos, none accepts a share from the Amazon.in or Flipkart Android apps, and pharmacy is near-zero (competitor_repos.tsv and GitHub searches).
- Flipkart search does have a skin-type facet ('Oily Skin', 'Dry Skin', 'Combination Skin', 'All Skin Types'), but the shopper has to know their type to use it. SkinKey fills it in from a measured scan.
- Existing tools each lack a piece: Skinimalist shares from Safari on iOS with a self-reported profile; Skin Bliss does a face scan and climate tips with no marketplace share-in; the desktop extensions (SkincareMate, GlowGuard, Clara) use self-entered profiles.

UNVERIFIED:
- That Amazon.in and Flipkart have no native skin-personalised filtering beyond Flipkart's manual facet.
- Nykaa reportedly launched an in-app 'Skin Scan' on 2025-11-18 (headline only). If that is accurate, Nykaa personalises only inside its own catalogue. SkinKey's point is that the profile works across stores and stays on the user's phone.
- No source shows that personalisation reduces waste or returns. Pitch it as a hypothesis.
core_flow:
ONBOARD / SKIN PROFILE (needed for everything else; built once)
1. A consent screen in plain language says:
   - one selfie is uploaded to YouCam for analysis;
   - YouCam keeps results for 24h (per the docs);
   - SkinKey deletes the photo from the phone right after the task and stores only derived scores;
   - nothing is shared unless the user creates a share link.
   There is an explicit 'I agree' and a 'skip, enter skin type manually' path.
2. Guided capture with expo-camera: frontal face, more than 60% of frame width, even light, with a 'move to daylight' hint.
3. The phone uploads through our small proxy (Cloudflare Worker, so the API key never ships in the app). The flow is POST /s2s/v2.0/file, then a presigned PUT, then Skin Analysis v2.1 SD and Facial Color Tones tasks, then polling.
4. Local storage (expo-secure-store / AsyncStorage) holds skin_type, per-concern ui_score for oiliness, moisture, redness, acne, pore, texture, radiance and dark_circle_v2, the skin_age band, the skin-tone hex and the scan date. Mask PNGs are shown once on the results screen and never saved. The photo is deleted.
5. A 'What we keep' screen lists the stored numbers and has a Delete button.
6. The UI shows bands (low / medium / high) rather than precise verdicts, with a fairness note: 'Skin AI can be less accurate on deeper skin tones and in poor light. Treat as a cosmetic guide; re-scan in daylight if it looks wrong.' The research cites Daneshjou 2022. An optional Fitzpatrick result is used only to show that note, never to change scores.

HERO / SHARE-TO-CHECK (the demo flow)
7. In the real Flipkart or Amazon.in Android app, the user taps Share on a product and picks SkinKey. The app is registered as an ACTION_SEND text/plain target via expo-share-intent 9.0.0 on Expo SDK 58, in a dev build.
8. useShareIntent() in the root layout provides text, webUrl and meta.title. A parser pulls out the amzn.in, amazon.in, dl.flipkart.com or flipkart.com link and treats the remaining text as the title. An editable 'Is this the product?' field covers shares that contain only a link. SkinKey never fetches the Amazon or Flipkart page.
9. Matching, deterministic:
   a) Fuzzy-match the title against a hand-built seed catalogue of about 30-40 common Indian skincare products. INCI lists are typed in from brand sites, with a source URL per row.
   b) If there is no match, use title keywords such as niacinamide, salicylic, SPF 50, oil-free, gel, 'for dry skin', 'rich cream' or fragrance, labelled 'based on product name only'.
   c) Otherwise the result is 'unknown, scan barcode in store or check the ingredient list'.
10. A rules table of about 30 actives, each row citing EU CosIng, maps actives to scores. Examples: high oiliness favours gel, oil-free, niacinamide and salicylic acid, and is cautioned against heavy occlusive creams; low moisture favours ceramide, hyaluronic acid and glycerin; high redness is cautioned against fragrance, alcohol denat. and strong acids.
11. Result card shows FITS, CAUTION or UNKNOWN. Every reason names the score that drove it, for example 'Your oiliness reading: high (scan 1 Nov)'. It also states the data source tier (catalogue / title-only) and uses cosmetic-only wording. There is a permanent 'not medical advice' line and a pharmacist/dermatologist link.
12. Buttons:
    - 'Back to product' reopens the original shared link.
    - 'Find better matches' opens a plain https search URL: the Flipkart skin_type facet plus query, or the Amazon.in or Nykaa keyword search (see marketplace_integration). If the store app is installed and claims the URL, it opens; otherwise the browser does.

SUPPORTING / SKIN FORECAST (light)
13. A Home card uses expo-location (or a city picker of about 20 hard-coded Indian cities) and calls Open-Meteo for uv_index_max, relative_humidity_2m and temperature_2m with timezone=auto.
14. About 8 rules combine weather with the profile, for example 'UV max 9 tomorrow: SPF 50, reapply' and 'Humidity 80% + high oiliness: switch to gel moisturiser'. A 'Travel kit' screen takes a city and dates within the forecast window and outputs a 5-item checklist. Each item links into the same 'Find better matches' builder.
15. The UV level also feeds the hero check: on a high-UV week, a missing SPF raises a caution for a day cream.

SUPPORTING / AISLE CHECK (light, reuses the hero result screen)
16. In a store, the user scans the product barcode with expo-camera. The app looks it up in the seed catalogue first, then Open Beauty Facts /api/v2/product/{barcode} with a proper User-Agent. A miss means UNKNOWN plus manual entry. The result is the same FITS / CAUTION / UNKNOWN card.
17. A referral checklist ('Is any of this true? painful, bleeding, spreading, a spot that changed fast, sudden rash') shows 'Please talk to the pharmacist or a dermatologist; this app only gives cosmetic guidance' instead of product advice. Very high redness or acne bands also add a soft 'consider a pharmacist or dermatologist' line, never a diagnosis.
18. 'Show to pharmacist' creates a revocable share:
    - The phone posts only the derived score bands and skin type, no image or hex, to the Worker KV under a random token with a 30-minute TTL.
    - It displays a QR code for https://skinkey.<domain>/p/<token>. The pharmacist opens it as a plain web page.
    - 'Revoke now' deletes the key, and a share log on the phone records when the profile was shared.
19. STRETCH (about 1h): Android App Links on our own domain, so the same /p/ link opens SkinKey when it is installed and the web page otherwise.
youcam_apis: File upload: POST /s2s/v2.0/file returns a presigned PUT URL; called through our proxy so the API key stays server-side

Skin Analysis v2.1 SD (skin_type, oiliness, moisture, redness, acne, pore, texture, radiance, dark_circle_v2): per-concern ui_score/raw_score, overall score, skin_age, mask PNG overlays shown once and not stored; 9-22 units per scan
Facial Color Tones analyzer (skin colour hex), used for the profile and the fairness/limits note
Fitzpatrick skin type (optional; only triggers the accuracy/limits caveat and never changes recommendations)

UNVERIFIED, check in hour 1: the exact enum values Skin Analysis returns for skin_type, which decide the mapping to Flipkart's 'Oily Skin' / 'Dry Skin' / 'Combination Skin' / 'All Skin Types', and whether a task or file deletion endpoint exists for early purge
marketplace_integration:
WHAT WE BUILD (only mechanisms the research verified as feasible)

A) SHARE-IN, from the Amazon.in or Flipkart app into SkinKey.
- The standard Android share target: an intent-filter for ACTION_SEND with category DEFAULT and mimeType text/plain, read from EXTRA_TEXT (VERIFIED, Android docs).
- Implemented with expo-share-intent 9.0.0 (VERIFIED on npm, released 2026-10-21):
  - peer dependencies are expo ^58, expo-linking >=58.0.13 and expo-constants >=58.0.12;
  - it needs a plugin entry plus scheme 'skinkey' in app.json;
  - useShareIntent() returns text, webUrl and meta.title (meta.title works on Android);
  - it does not run in Expo Go, so a dev build is required (eas build -p android --profile development or expo run:android).
- Not verified:
  - what the shared text actually contains (title plus amzn.in/d/... or dl.flipkart.com/s/... is likely but UNVERIFIED);
  - whether each marketplace app hands off to the generic Android chooser (UNVERIFIED).
  Test this on a real phone in the first 15 minutes.
- Fallbacks: an editable title field, then following the redirect on the phone to pull the ASIN after /dp/ or the Flipkart pid= value (that pattern is UNVERIFIED), then manual entry.
- Server-side link resolution is unreliable: a Flipkart short link returned 504/500 to curl in our own test. We never fetch or scrape product pages. Flipkart's terms ban page-scraping and robots, and amazon.in's robots.txt disallows the common bots.

B) LINK-OUT, plain https search URLs that we build. No API and no affiliate tags.
- Flipkart, VERIFIED (HTTP 200, and the page's facetMap showed the filter applied):
  https://www.flipkart.com/search?q=<skin-matched terms>&p%5B%5D=facets.skin_type%255B%255D%3D<Oily%2BSkin|Dry%2BSkin|Combination%2BSkin|All%2BSkin%2BTypes>
  These parameters are undocumented and could change, so the app checks the facet and falls back to a q-only URL.
- Nykaa, PARTLY VERIFIED: https://www.nykaa.com/search/result/?q=<terms> works. The skin-type filter syntax is UNVERIFIED, so we use keywords only.
- Amazon.in, UNVERIFIED (amazon.in returned 503 to our fetchers): https://www.amazon.in/s?k=<terms>&i=beauty. There is no skin-type parameter, so the skin terms go into k.
- Opening the native app:
  - The domains publish assetlinks.json for in.amazon.mShop.android.shopping, com.flipkart.android and com.fsn.nykaa (VERIFIED at domain level). Whether search paths open in-app on Android is UNVERIFIED, so test on a phone.
  - On iOS, Flipkart claims all paths and Amazon.in claims /s and /dp/ (VERIFIED), though iOS is out of scope.
  - If the store app isn't installed, the browser opens. We open URLs with Linking.openURL, not a WebView; Amazon's rule 21 bans WebViews for approved apps, so we avoid them entirely.

C) OUR OWN LINKS OPEN OUR APP. Expo docs verified this; it is a stretch goal.
- https://skinkey.<domain>/p/<token> (pharmacist share) and /l/<token> (a shareable skin-matched shopping list).
- Android App Links need: android.intentFilters with autoVerify true, scheme https, our host and pathPrefix /p and /l; and public/.well-known/assetlinks.json served as application/json with our package name plus the SHA256 fingerprint from 'eas credentials -p android'.
- Without the app, the same URL is a plain web page showing the derived bands, or the list with plain store search links. Making that full fallback flow work is our design choice, not documented Expo behaviour.

WHAT IS NOT POSSIBLE (say so plainly in the pitch and README)
- We cannot make Amazon or Flipkart links, or their apps, open SkinKey. Their link files list only their own apps.
- We cannot add a SkinKey button, overlay or filter inside the Amazon or Flipkart apps.
- We cannot change their results or add filters beyond what their URLs already accept: Flipkart's skin_type, brand and discount facets, and keyword-only search on Amazon and Nykaa.
- We cannot read ingredient lists from their pages or APIs:
  - Amazon PA-API 5 is deprecated in favour of the Creators API, which needs an approved Associates account plus 10 qualifying sales in 30 days and has no ingredients field;
  - the Flipkart Affiliate API needs a token, sign-ups have reportedly been paused since 2018, and it has no ingredients field.
- We cannot use affiliate links in the hackathon app, because Amazon Associates India mobile apps need separate approval.
- We cannot show Amazon reviews or ratings (Associates rule 28) or use Amazon or Flipkart logos, which could imply a partnership.
mobile_native_angle:
The integration only works on a phone:
- SkinKey is a system share-sheet target inside the native Flipkart and Amazon.in apps, which is where Indian shoppers actually browse. A web app or desktop extension cannot do this; zdress, for example, is a desktop extension.
- It hands off to the native store apps through their verified App Links domains.
- It uses on-device secure storage for the derived-scores-only profile.
- It uses camera capture with framing checks for the scan and barcode scanning in the aisle.
- It uses device location for the forecast and shows an in-person QR to a pharmacist.
Android-first in an Expo SDK 58 dev build. The research puts the iOS share extension at 3-5 more hours plus provisioning, so iOS is explicitly deferred. Very few competitor repos are native mobile apps (evidence.md).
novelty_vs_competitors:
Each piece exists somewhere; the combination does not, based on 356 hackathon repos and the consumer apps checked. The absence is verified only within that search and is not a full market scan.

The new part is a measured YouCam skin profile used from inside the Flipkart and Amazon.in Android apps through the share sheet, returning reasoned fit or caution plus a pre-filtered Flipkart skin_type search.

Closest alternatives:
- Skinimalist: shares a link from Safari on iOS, but the profile is self-reported and it is iOS-only.
- Skin Bliss: face scan, barcode, climate/UV/humidity tips, but no marketplace share-in.
- Haut.AI Skin.Chat: selfie to Amazon links, outbound only.
- Desktop extensions (SkincareMate, GlowGuard, Clara by Clinikally): self-entered profiles, desktop only.
- zdress: Flipkart/Amazon extension for clothing try-on, no skin analysis.
- ShelfSense: a localStorage 'Skin Passport' that can't be shared with stores, hence our rename.
- Parasol: weather-based travel skin forecast on Shopify.
- skin-to-shelf: outbound Google Shopping.
- Nykaa Skin Scan: reportedly in-app and tied to Nykaa's own catalogue (UNVERIFIED).

The second new part is a revocable, derived-scores-only profile handed to a pharmacist by QR with a 30-minute TTL. No repo or product checked offers this.

Not new, so pitched as supporting features: weather tips (Skin Bliss, Parasol), barcode checks (ShelfSense, Yuka, Think Dirty), and pharmacy plus skin AI (Amazon Milan Derma-bar).

It follows the Round 1 winner pattern: every claim traceable to a ui_score (as in Aloud), deterministic auditable rules, honesty guardrails, and a shipped APK.
demo_wow_moment:
This is screen-recorded on a real Android phone (60-75 seconds of the 1-3 minute video):
1. The presenter is in the real Flipkart app on a 'rich' moisturising cream, taps Share and picks SkinKey.
2. Within about 2 seconds SkinKey shows CAUTION: 'Your oiliness reading: HIGH (scan 1 Nov). This product's ingredient list (brand site, catalogue) is cream-based with heavy occlusives. UV max 9 in Delhi tomorrow and no SPF listed.' The card shows the source tier and a 'cosmetic guidance, not medical advice' line.
3. The presenter taps 'Find better matches on Flipkart'. The Flipkart app opens with the 'Oily Skin' skin-type filter already applied and the query 'oil-free gel moisturiser niacinamide'. The filter is one the shopper would never have known to set.
4. The presenter repeats the share from the Amazon.in app and gets the same verdict, then opens a keyword search.
5. A cutaway shows the 'What we keep' screen: about 10 numbers, a date, no photo, and a Delete button. Then the in-store barcode scan, the referral checklist, and a pharmacist QR that the presenter revokes live, with the web page switching to 'This profile was revoked'.
Fallback if Flipkart's facet or app hand-off breaks on the day: show the browser version of the same URL (already verified at HTTP 200 with the facet applied).
risks:
Share payload (UNVERIFIED)
- The Amazon.in or Flipkart share may contain only a short link, or the app may not offer the generic chooser.
- Mitigation: the phone test in the first hour, an editable title, redirect-following on the phone to get the ASIN or pid, and manual entry.
- If share-in fails entirely, the hero falls back to paste-link or barcode. The pitch would weaken, so test first.

Facet and App Link behaviour
- Flipkart's skin_type facet is undocumented and could change. Whether search URLs open in the native apps is UNVERIFIED (only domain-level assetlinks are verified). Amazon's /s?k= format is UNVERIFIED.
- Mitigation: q-only fallback URLs, and browser fallback is acceptable.

Legal
- Flipkart's terms prohibit 'deep-link, page-scrape, robot, spider or other automatic device' access. We read this as banning automated access, not a user tapping a search link, but that reading is our own interpretation and not legal advice (UNVERIFIED).
- Amazon: no Associates tags, no WebViews, no logos, no reviews or ratings, and no price tracking.
- Open-Meteo's free tier is non-commercial only; the hackathon demo is our own reading of that.
- Open Beauty Facts data is ODbL, with attribution and share-alike, and its terms say it must not be used for medical purposes. That matches our cosmetic-only stance.

Weak matching
- Title-only matching is weak, and Open Beauty Facts covers only 348 India-tagged products with complete ingredients.
- Mitigation: a hand-built seed catalogue, a source tier on every verdict, and an honest UNKNOWN state. The catalogue is labour-intensive, so cap it at 25-40 products.

Skin AI accuracy and bias
- Lighting and darker skin tones affect accuracy (Daneshjou 2022).
- Mitigation: bands rather than verdict scores, a limits note, a re-scan prompt, Fitzpatrick used only for the caveat, and a manual skin-type override.

Privacy and BIPA-style exposure
- The face image must go to YouCam servers, which keep results 24h per the docs. Whether a deletion endpoint exists is UNVERIFIED.
- Mitigation: explicit e-consent, a published retention statement, deleting the local photo immediately, never storing mask PNGs or linking face data to identity, and never uploading shared product text together with face data.
- The pharmacist share sends only derived bands, with a TTL and revocation.

Medical framing
- Copy must stay cosmetic ('looks oily', not 'treats acne'), with a referral checklist and a permanent not-medical-advice line. A copy lint pass before the demo is in scope.

Build and time
- The dev build is required (no Expo Go) and EAS queue times can be long. Start the build early and keep local expo run:android as a backup.
- iOS is deferred.
- 9-22 API units per scan: cache one demo scan.

Novelty and positioning
- If Nykaa's Skin Scan is real, India's main beauty retailer already personalises its own catalogue. Our angle is a portable, on-phone, cross-store profile.
- The 'Skin Passport' name clashes with ShelfSense, hence the rename to SkinKey (trademark search for SkinKey not done, UNVERIFIED).
